business_conventions.fictional_scope: DemoRetail directly sold ordinary physical goods, paid by card. No live backend access and no autonomous transaction actions.
business_conventions.calendar_days: Consecutive local dates including weekends. Event date is day zero; the next date is day one. A window includes its final day and expires at the end of that day.
business_conventions.business_days: Monday through Friday, with no holiday calendar in this fictional benchmark. Event date is excluded, next eligible weekday is day one; deadline expires at end of final business day.
business_conventions.unknown_dates: Ask for the relevant date; never infer that a deadline passed. Do not block urgent security or missing-parcel review on missing optional dates.
business_conventions.dispatch: First physical carrier acceptance; label creation is not dispatch.
business_conventions.refund_approval: An authorized reviewer explicitly approves a refund; request, return authorization and warehouse receipt are not approval.
business_conventions.amounts: Pre-dispatch confirmed cancellation: full order payment including delivery. Verified duplicate capture: extra captured amount. Ordinary compliant return: paid item price excluding original delivery; customer pays return postage. Item-problem remedy amount is set explicitly by the authorized reviewer; prepaid return if required. The assistant never calculates, approves or transfers money.
business_conventions.priority: Security and high-risk action controls first; policy conflicts stop advice. Specific state overrides general tracking/delay/return handling. Missing decisive facts prompt clarification. Multiple clearly applicable issues permit reviewed multi-card guidance, not forced single-card answers.
business_conventions.review: All outputs are drafts. No generated response is automatically sent. A human can inspect full cards, uncertainty and version and reject the guidance.

policies.title: Password and login recovery
policies.supported_issue: Unable to sign in or reset a forgotten password.
policies.short_description: Ordinary access recovery when there is no reported security restriction or unfamiliar activity.
policies.policy_text: For a forgotten password or ordinary sign-in failure, guide the customer to the password-recovery option on the DemoRetail sign-in page. The customer completes recovery privately using the registered contact channel. Check the exact error and whether that channel is accessible before suggesting another recovery attempt. If a requested recovery message has not arrived after 15 minutes, suggest checking filtered mail once; if still absent, refer for access review rather than repeated attempts. A reported security lock or unfamiliar access takes priority over ordinary recovery.
eligibility_conditions: The customer describes a sign-in or password problem.
No security lock or suspected compromise is reported.
The registered contact channel is accessible for self-service recovery.

policies.short_description: Security review takes precedence over routine login recovery when a lock or compromise is reported.
policies.policy_text: Treat a reported security lock, unfamiliar sign-in or unauthorized account change as a security-review case. Pause ordinary recovery guidance that could bypass the restriction and direct the customer to a human security review through the existing DemoRetail support channel. A reviewer must establish identity through the approved private process before any account change. The assistant may explain the review route but cannot verify identity, confirm a breach or unlock access. Do not impose a waiting period before reporting a security concern.

policies.title: Cancellation before dispatch
policies.supported_issue: A customer wants to stop an order before it leaves the retailer.
policies.short_description: A cancellation request is reviewable before carrier acceptance; a shipping label alone does not prove dispatch.
policies.policy_text: An order may be submitted for cancellation while it has not been accepted by a carrier. Dispatch means the carrier's first physical acceptance, not label creation. The representative must check current dispatch state before confirming cancellation; a customer report alone is not confirmation. If cancellation is confirmed before handoff, a captured payment is referred for a full order-payment refund, including any original delivery charge. An authorization that is still pending is handled as a hold, not as a captured-payment refund. Once the refund is formally approved, the standard 5-business-day receipt window applies. Cancellation is never guaranteed while verification is pending.
eligibility_conditions: The request is to stop an existing order.
Carrier acceptance has not occurred and must be verified before cancellation confirmation.

policies.supported_issue: A customer asks to cancel an order already handed to the carrier.
policies.short_description: After dispatch, explain the return route rather than promising to stop the shipment.
policies.policy_text: Once a carrier has physically accepted the parcel, standard cancellation is unavailable. Do not promise interception or advise refusal of delivery as a guaranteed refund route. If the customer still wants to return an ordinary item after receipt, explain that a separate eligibility review can take place within 14 calendar days after delivery, with the delivery day excluded from the count. That future return remains subject to the ordinary condition requirements; this card does not itself approve it. A parcel that never arrives or an item arriving damaged needs its corresponding delivery or item-remedy review.
eligibility_conditions: The primary request is cancellation.
Carrier acceptance has occurred.

policies.short_description: Review confirmed lateness without assuming the parcel is lost.

After that window ends, a representative may request a carrier status check. If there is still no delivery by the end of 3 business days after the promised window's final date, escalate for a delivery investigation. Lateness alone does not establish loss or grant a refund. A reported carrier loss or a delivered scan disputed by the recipient goes directly to missing-parcel review without waiting for the 3-business-day threshold.

Ask whether household members or an agreed safe location have been checked only where safe and relevant; do not require the customer to confront neighbours or obtain sensitive evidence. Record the discrepancy and the delivery reference for an authorized reviewer. No waiting period is required before opening this review. Neither a delivered scan nor a customer's use of the word lost alone proves liability, final loss or refund eligibility. Any replacement or reimbursement is a separate human decision after investigation.

If the promised delivery window has already ended, prioritize the delayed-delivery procedure; if loss or disputed delivery is reported, prioritize missing-parcel review. policies.title: Failed payment attempt
policies.supported_issue: Checkout reports that a payment attempt failed.
policies.short_description: Review a failed attempt while checking whether funds are pending or captured before another attempt.
policies.policy_text: A failed checkout message does not prove that no funds were reserved. Ask the customer to distinguish failed, pending and posted payment status using a safe description from their payment record. If no authorization or captured payment is shown and no order confirmation exists, basic checks of entered non-secret billing information and a single later checkout attempt may be suggested. Do not advise repeated retries. If there is a pending hold, use authorization guidance; if funds are posted or an order confirmation exists despite the failure message, obtain payment review before suggesting another payment.
eligibility_conditions: A payment attempt is reported failed.
Pending or captured funds and order confirmation must be checked before any suggestion to retry.

policies.title: Pending payment or authorization hold
policies.supported_issue: A payment is pending or a temporary authorization is still visible.
policies.short_description: An unsettled payment hold is not the same as a duplicate captured charge or an approved refund.
policies.policy_text: For a card authorization still marked pending, explain that a reservation is not a confirmed captured payment. In this fictional service, a pending authorization is expected to clear or update within 5 business days after its authorization date. If it remains pending after that window, refer to an authorized payment reviewer; actual release depends on the payment provider and must not be guaranteed. When one entry is captured and another pending, review the pending entry as a hold rather than automatically declaring a duplicate capture. A refund approved by DemoRetail uses the refund-approval date and refund-status procedure instead.

policies.supported_issue: Two posted payments appear to relate to one order.
policies.short_description: Review possible duplicate capture instead of assuming every second bank entry is a completed charge.
policies.policy_text: A suspected duplicate-payment case requires two posted or captured entries for the same DemoRetail purchase. An authorized representative checks order and transaction records before confirming duplication. If a duplicate capture is verified, the reviewer can approve reversal of the extra captured amount only; the assistant does not issue it. After formal refund approval, allow the standard 5-business-day receipt window. One posted entry plus a pending hold is not sufficient to confirm a duplicate capture and belongs to pending-payment review. Two distinct valid orders are not automatically duplicates.

Duplication must be verified before any refund approval.

policies.title: Standard return and refund eligibility
policies.supported_issue: A customer wants to know whether an ordinary delivered item can be returned for a refund.
policies.short_description: Standard return eligibility depends on receipt date and item condition, not simply the refund category.
policies.policy_text: An ordinary change-of-mind return can be requested within 14 calendar days after delivery, excluding the delivery day and including the final day. The item must be unused, unaltered and complete with its original packaging and accessories. After a representative authorizes the return, the customer must dispatch it within 7 calendar days after authorization, excluding that day. Standard return postage is the customer's responsibility. A compliant return refunds the paid item price, not the original delivery charge. Refund approval follows inspection, targeted within 3 business days after warehouse receipt; missing inspection beyond that point requires review, not automatic approval. After approval, the receipt window is 5 business days.
eligibility_conditions: Ordinary delivered goods are being returned for change of mind.
The request is within 14 calendar days after delivery.
The item is unused, unaltered and complete with original packaging and accessories.
Dispatch occurs within 7 calendar days after return authorization.

policies.title: Approved refund not yet received
policies.supported_issue: A refund was formally approved but the customer has not received it.
policies.short_description: Track an existing refund outcome using approval date, not the date a return was requested.
policies.policy_text: For a formally approved refund, the expected receipt window is 5 business days after the approval date, excluding that date. Count from the approval notice, not the cancellation request, return dispatch, warehouse receipt or original payment date. Within the window, explain the processing period without claiming that a provider has settled funds. After the window ends, prepare a payment trace for an authorized representative. An approval reference is evidence to verify, not a guarantee of bank receipt. Refunds use the original payment route; a request to redirect funds requires review and is never executed by the assistant.
eligibility_conditions: DemoRetail refund approval is reported and can be identified.
The primary issue is non-receipt of that refund.
Approval date is needed before declaring it overdue.

policies.title: Damaged or incorrect item remedy
policies.supported_issue: A delivered item is damaged or differs from what was ordered.
policies.short_description: Item-problem review has its own evidence and timing rules, separate from an ordinary unused-item return.
policies.policy_text: Ask the customer to report visible damage or incorrect contents within 7 calendar days after delivery, excluding the delivery day. Keep the item and packaging where safe; photographs are optional supporting evidence and must not be a barrier where unavailable or unsafe. An authorized reviewer decides a refund or replacement after checking the order and problem. The ordinary unused-item condition does not disqualify a damage report simply because the item was opened for inspection. If a return is required, the retailer provides a prepaid return route; dispatch is due within 7 calendar days after return authorization. For a refund, approval normally follows inspection within 3 business days after warehouse receipt. The reviewer may explicitly waive the return and approve a remedy earlier. An approved refund follows the 5-business-day receipt window.
eligibility_conditions: The parcel was received and the contents are damaged or incorrect.
The ordinary reporting window is 7 calendar days after delivery.
A representative verifies the issue and decides the remedy; no automatic refund is promised.

policies.title: Customer requests a human representative
policies.supported_issue: The customer explicitly asks to speak with a representative.
policies.short_description: Respect a request for human contact even when an ordinary support procedure could apply.
policies.policy_text: When a customer asks for a person, prepare a concise handoff through the existing DemoRetail support channel. Ask for a short issue summary only if it is not already clear; do not require them to repeat the whole conversation. Explain the fictional service target of a first representative response within 2 business days after a case is actually accepted into the support queue. The assistant cannot submit a case or verify queue acceptance, so the target must be conditional and is not a guaranteed appointment. Security concerns use immediate security routing rather than being told to wait for the routine target.
eligibility_conditions: The customer explicitly requests a human representative.
A handoff preference can be honored without establishing that the substantive issue is unsupported.

policies.title: Unsupported, conflicting or complex-case review
policies.supported_issue: A reviewer needs a structured handoff for an unresolved case.
policies.short_description: Procedural guidance for documenting scope gaps, conflicting facts or multiple unresolved issues; not a substantive answer.
policies.policy_text: Use this handoff procedure only after the workflow has established that no substantive approved policy applies, material facts remain contradictory after a safe clarification, or several unresolved issues require coordinated review. Summarize the customer's objective, facts as reported, unresolved questions and any relevant policy boundaries. Keep conflicting statements separate. Refer the summary through the existing support channel for an authorized reviewer; the normal first-response target is 2 business days after confirmed queue acceptance. This procedure supplies no eligibility, payment or delivery rule and must not be substituted for a relevant substantive card solely because it is the nearest text match.
eligibility_conditions: A scope gap, unresolved material contradiction or need for coordinated review has already been identified.
The requested output is a handoff summary, not an invented substantive policy answer.
